title: Kingdom of Afghanistan
capsule: The Kingdom of Afghanistan was proclaimed in 1926 when Amanullah Khan converted the emirate to a kingdom following his European tour and launched a modernization program — secularizing education, reforming dress codes, and promoting women's public life — that provoked a tribal and Islamist uprising; he abdicated in January 1929. After a brief civil war, Mohammad Nadir Shah seized the throne, consolidated order by reversing Amanullah's reforms, and was assassinated in 1933, leaving his 19-year-old son Mohammad Zahir Shah to reign for 40 years (1933–1973) during which Afghanistan maintained Cold War neutrality and received development aid from both superpowers. On 17 July 1973 Zahir Shah was deposed in a bloodless coup by his cousin Mohammad Daoud Khan while the king was abroad, ending the monarchy and establishing a republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's national territory is well documented; the Durand Line with British India/Pakistan (1893) and borders with the Soviet Union were formally established, though the Durand Line has never been formally recognized as an international border by successive Afghan governments.
